$comment: Cross-fragment proposals from the QA pass over data/35-logic.json (mb.logic, the merchant 74-series glue logic). Nothing here has been applied: the fragment now references the canonical nodes by id and no longer inlines its own copies. What remains is (a) merges into nodes this agent does not own, (b) id renames, and (c) the factual drift found between the inlined copies and the published ones, which the maintainer may want to fold in. Every merge below was already applied on the 35-logic side - the copy is gone and the reference is in place - so applying these is about tidying the other fragment, not about unblocking the build.

merges.why: The whole point of this pass. This node used to inline the entire silicon-from-quartz chain as 30 of its own nodes - quartzite, coke, the submerged-arc furnace, metallurgical silicon, the Siemens reactor, polysilicon, hydrochloric acid, brine, rock salt, the hydrogen-from-natural-gas reformer and the gas field, the Czochralski puller, crucible, seed, saw, lap, polish, wafer sizes and die-per-wafer. All of it now hangs off si.wafer by id. Note that si.wafer is written as a 100 mm wafer; a merchant bipolar logic line of 1983 also ran 75 mm entry lines, so if si.wafer is to be the canonical wafer for the whole tree its note should say so - it currently mentions 75 mm only in passing, in the context of discretes. The 75 mm fact is carried in 35-logic.json on mb.logic.bipolar.wafer for now.

renames.why: ALREADY APPLIED by the 10-silicon.json agent during this pass; recorded because 35-logic now depends on the new id. Flagging the consequence: si.wafer is a 100 mm wafer, but a merchant bipolar logic line of 1983 also ran 75 mm entry lines, so if si.wafer is meant to be the canonical wafer for the whole tree its note should say so (it currently mentions 75 mm only in passing, in the context of discretes). No rename is being requested here.

OPTIONAL, not required. metal.silica is named 'High-purity silicon feedstock (9N polysilicon)' and is used as the canonical 'silicon' ingredient by roughly thirty nodes, but it also carries a child called metal.silica.quartz-crystal, '2.048 MHz quartz clock crystal', which is a mechanical resonator and not silicon at all - a quartz crystal is grown hydrothermally from silica, but it is not a branch of the silicon feedstock chain. Two unrelated things are currently in one node. Splitting the clock crystal out, or renaming the parent, would remove a genuine mis-parenting.

aliases.why: Roughly six nodes across 10-silicon and 30-passives have inputs: ['silicon']. Until this pass those resolved by name to mb.logic.economics.bill.silicon, a note about 3 mg of die silicon, which is not what any of them meant. With that node gone the string resolves to nothing. metal.silica is the right target.

About twelve nodes across 10-silicon, 40-chassis and 50-power have inputs: ['aluminium'] (British spelling). These were resolving to mb.logic.economics.bill.aluminium, a note about on-die metal; they now resolve to nothing. metal.aluminum is the right target, and the alias also removes the aluminium/aluminum split that has been quietly producing two different destinations for one substance.

About twelve nodes across 30-passives, 40-chassis, 60-metals and 90-peripherals have inputs: ['air']. These were resolving by name to mb.logic.cmos.process.locos.nitride.ammonia.nitrogen.air, a three-line stub; with it gone the string resolves to nothing. facility.nitrogen.atmospheric-air is what most of them mean. The ones that mean process air rather than nitrogen are a judgement call the maintainer may want to make per node.

mb.cpu.wafer.blade and mb.cpu.dice-tool in 10-silicon.json have inputs: ['industrial diamond'], which resolved by name to mb.logic.bipolar.wafer.saw.diamond. That node is deleted, so those two edges are now prose. The string should resolve to si.wafer.diamond.
facility.water.sulphuric-acid in 80-industry.json had an input string matching the deleted mb.logic.bipolar.litho.strip.piranha.sulphuric.sulphur. chem.sulfur is the canonical sulphur.

Two nodes in 40-chassis and 80-industry had input strings matching the deleted mb.logic.bipolar.process.epi.phosphine.phosphorus.phosphate. The canonical phosphate rock node is the phosphorus-source one; metal.phosphate-ore is a near-duplicate of it and is itself a merge candidate.

drift.finding: 10-silicon.json and 60-metals.json contradict each other. si.polysilicon is titled '9N-11N electronic-grade polysilicon' with a fact 'Purity: 9N-11N (99.9999999%)'; metal.silica says '9N-11N for modern polysilicon; 6N-7N typical of the 1982 era'. The deleted 35-logic copy sided with 10-silicon ('9-11 nines'). The metals fragment is closer to right: semiconductor-grade polysilicon in the early 1980s was around 6N-9N, with 9N-11N a figure for later decades. Suggest settling on '6N-9N in 1983, 9N-11N by the late 1990s' and correcting si.polysilicon's title, which is currently the most prominent and the least accurate of the three.

The deleted 35-logic copy said argon over the melt; si.cz.atmosphere says helium, and its own note concedes that 'argon or a helium/argon mix was a cheaper alternative and produced more oxygen precipitation'. Both were used and the note already covers it. No change needed - recorded so nobody reads the deletion as a correction.

si.polysilicon.saf is 'Submerged arc furnace, 20-40 MVA'; si.polysilicon.msi's description says 1900-2200 C. The deleted 35-logic copy said ~1800-2000 C, which is the figure usually quoted for the carbon arc bath. 1900-2200 C is high but not absurd for the electrode tips. Worth a look, low stakes.

metal.silica ('High-purity silicon feedstock') has metal.silica.quartz-crystal ('2.048 MHz quartz clock crystal') as a child. A quartz crystal is grown hydrothermally from silica but is a mechanical resonator for the VIC-II's colour subcarrier reference, not a stage in making silicon wafers. It should not sit under silicon feedstock. See the renames section.

The deleted 35-logic node described trichloroethylene as '1,1,1-trichloroethane family'. That is a different compound. 1,1,2-trichloroethene, CHCl=CCl2, boiling at 87 C, is the right identity and chem.solvents.trichloroethylene already has it. Recording it because it is the only factual error found in this fragment that was not a copy of somebody else's correct node.

The deleted 35-logic copy carried a fact reading 'Dopant: arsenic (p-type) or phosphorus (n-type)'. Arsenic is a donor, so that is backwards: p-type is boron or gallium, n-type is phosphorus or arsenic. si.cz is correctly titled 'Czochralski growth of the boron-doped ingot'. The error is gone with the node; recording it because it is the kind of thing that gets copy-pasted.

note: Fragment summary: 228 nodes before this pass, 129 after. 100 nodes were deleted, 1 added (mb.logic.sourcing.makers.signetics, split out of a node that had absorbed two companies into one). Forty of those deletions were inlined duplicates of nodes published in 10-silicon.json, 60-metals.json and 70-petrochem.json; ten were the economics bill/labour/price subtree, folded into one note; eight were bare processes with no children and no ingredients; one was a duplicated photomask bay; the rest were folded into their parents' descriptions, facts or notes. Mechanical audit for this fragment: 4 FAIL and 146 WARN before, 0 FAIL and 7 WARN after - build.mjs, audit.mjs --file 35-logic.json and selftest.mjs all exit 0. The 7 remaining WARNs are all r3 category objections that I accepted deliberately and documented in the nodes' own notes: five `tool` under `packaging` (a progressive die set, a transfer press, a wire bonder, a probe station and a logic tester are capital equipment and there is no machine-tool category), and two `note` under `packaging` and `logistics`. The other 33 WARNs the file-scoped audit prints are r4 duplicate-name rows in which no id from this fragment appears; they belong to 10-silicon, 20-board, 30-passives, 40-chassis, 60-metals, 70-petrochem, 80-industry and 90-peripherals. This fragment's own eleven `children` edges onto facility.water and facility.electricity have all been moved to `from` per rule 1a, and it now contributes no r1a edge at all. Two things a maintainer should know before applying the proposals above: several of the deleted nodes were acting as unintended name hubs for other fragments' ingredient strings - about twenty nodes resolved 'phosphine' to mb.logic.bipolar.process.epi.phosphine, about fifteen resolved 'ammonia' to the CMOS nitride node, and about six and twelve resolved 'silicon' and 'aluminium' to the two deleted economics bill nodes - and those edges now fall through to the canonical nodes, which is the right outcome but will move the tree's ingredient-link statistics.
